The presented BC incorporates a fully bridgeless bidirectional single stage isolated SEPIC AC-DC converter to enable effective power transfer between grid and battery packs through G2V and V2G operation. Notably, the discontinuous current mode design of the presented BC enables zero current switching of semiconductor devices. It eliminates the supply current sensor requirement, guaranteeing simple and low-cost control implementation. The presented BC exhibits unity power factor operation and limited harmonics distortions at AC mains while transferring power between AC mains and battery packs, i.e., under both G2V and V2G mode operation. Further, low device count, simple control architecture, and isolation features demonstrate the excellent suitability of presented BC in LVEVs charging applications. The operating principle, design, and control of the presented BC are discussed in detail, and finally, its performance is validated through a simulation study. The relevant results are presented for verifying the bidirectional BC performance as an LVEVs charger.

Author Keywords: and Bidirectional Bridgeless SEPIC AC-DC Converter

articleTitle: Circuit Averaging Approach to Model Two-Switch Battery Integrated DC/DC Converters for Interaction Analysis
abstract: This paper presents the small-signal modeling for stability and interaction analysis of the two-switch battery integrated converters used for integration of renewable energy source, DC load, and energy storage device. Based on the developed small-signal model using the circuit averaging technique, the interaction between the two-control loop formed by two switches of the battery integrated converter is revealed. Also, a detailed derivation of the unified small-signal impedance model is presented for analysis of the stability issue due to mutual interaction between the battery integrated converters and constant power load. The simulation results verify the theoretical findings.

Author Keywords: Load voltage regulation (LVR). Battery pulse charging scenario (BPCS)

articleTitle: Probabilistic Analysis of Wind Integrated Power System Considering 3-phase Line Fault
abstract: The uncertainties of energy systems are getting more and more attention as a direct response to energy system reorganisation on the one hand and exceptional renewable energy consumption on the other. Due to the increased difficulty of decision-making in the setting of the power system, it appears necessary to analyse the system’s performance level of uncertainty. Probabilistic methods must be applied to deal with uncertainty. In most engineering system studies, uncertainties can be represented probabilistically or possibilistically. Next to solar energy, wind energy will play a significant role in the creation of electricity. These sources, however, differ from traditional sources in behaviour and are unstable and fluctuating in energy. Using the model for a wind-integrated power system, which incorporates a three-phase fault, To assess the overall reliability of the system, the Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) approach is used. The static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) has been considered to minimise the fault latency. To keep the system’s parameters within desirable ranges, the task also includes the implementation of a STATCOM as a compensator at the point of common coupling. The MCS method is then applied to determine the system’s overall reliability. The MCS method configures the impedance of STATCOM, which helps mitigate the fault during its occurrence and achieve the expected system parameters during a 3-phase fault. In order to understand the advantages and disadvantages of different techniques, this study provides a comprehensive assessment of approaches to modelling uncertainty for power system research.

articleTitle: Improved One Cycle Control Strategy to Eliminate Steady State Error in Buck Regulators
abstract: One Cycle Control (OCC) is a non-linear switching strategy, which has the advantage of fast dynamic response and disturbance rejection. However, in spite of its several advantages, OCC has some limitations, such as finite reset time, dependency on integration accuracy etc. One typical limitation of OCC is that the output voltage may have a steady state error with respect to the reference. This paper addresses this issue, and proposes a simple and cost-effective solution for eliminating such steady state errors. This technique does not use any current sensor, works on only voltage sensing, and is effective over the entire load range of the converter. The technique is analyzed, a design method is proposed, and then the design is validated through simulation and experiments. The results prove the effectiveness of this strategy.

articleTitle: ATLHCAF and DMNGI-PLL Based Control Algorithms for a Dual-Stage SPV and BES in Shipboard Microgrid
abstract: Integrating renewable energy sources (RES) in the maritime industry is an efficient technique to decrease the pollution of water resources. This paper evaluates the functioning of the shipboard microgrid under varied operating situations. A microgrid comprising a solar photovoltaic array (SPV), battery, service loads, and propulsion motors is built and tested in the MATLAB-Simulink platform. The inclusion of propulsion motors and RES with power-electronic converter interfaces, leads to severe power quality concerns. Thus, an arctangent logarithmic hyperbolic cosine adaptive filter (ATLHCAF) is applied in the first voltage source converter (VSC) to enhance the system’s power quality. A dual modified novel generalized integrator-phase locked loop (DMNGI-PLL) is utilized for rapid and precise synchronization when the ship is at the port. A battery energy device (BES) is used in the ship owing to the intermittent nature of the SPV array. Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is applied for tuning the PI (Proportional Integer) controller to ensure the DC bus stability. Due to the complexity of numerous power source coordination and varying propulsion loads, a power management system (PMS) is crucial in planning and operating procedures.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Limiting at TSO-DSO Interface using Distribution Flexibility
abstract: A vast integration of distributed energy resources at the distribution level has emerged the system security issues such as voltage and frequency control for system operators. TSO and DSO have to initiate new grid policies to increase the coordination among the system operators. One of the needs for coordination is reactive power provision at the T-D interface to mitigate the probability of voltage violations. This manuscript proposes a new method to aggregate the reactive power at the T-D interface considering grid network and operational constraints using the distribution side flexibility. The impact of demand and Q/P ratio on the reactive power transfer is investigated to simulate the high DER integrated scenario. Results are validated using the modified IEEE 33 bus system. Furthermore, the effect of the Q/P ratio on the voltage at the primary substation node is also illustrated. Overall, this manuscript proposes the idea of reactive power management at the T-D interface and their affecting factors using the coordination between TSO and DSO, which will provide the direction for new grid initiatives for system operators.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Power Flow Control of Single Phase Matrix Converter Based Inductive WPT System for E-Vehicle Applications
abstract: A closed loop controller is presented to control the average grid power of series-series compensated inductive wireless power transfer (IWPT) using single phase matrix converter (SPMC). The controller enables the bidirectional power flow control between the EV battery and ac mains. SPMC can replace the conventional two stage ac to ac converter which consist two H-bridge and bulky dc link capacitor. It makes system compact and less space consuming. Based on the mathematical analysis linear modulation technique is used to eliminate grid harmonics which ensure high quality of grid current with high power factor in both G2V and V2G mode. This paper present circuit analysis and control technique. Verification of control technique has been done through MATLAB simulation which shows the UPF operation and 1.30% THD in grid current at rated power of 1 kW.

articleTitle: PI-Based Feedback Control Technique for Current Control of the Battery Energy Storage System
abstract: A reliable and robust battery current controller mitigates the load transient issues during the mode change and ensures the charging-discharging cycle properly, with improvement in the life cycle of the battery. Minimizing the overshoot, rise time, and settling time with maintaining the DC-link voltage during the load change is crucially important in the field of battery charging. In general, a PI controller is usually used to overcome these challenges. However, a traditional PI controller is suitable for a specific configuration, but it is observed that overshoot and oscillation happen when the load varies. In this paper, a PI-Based Feedback control technique for current control of the battery energy storage system (BESS) is presented. This modified feedback-based proportional and integral (PI) controller is designed to ensure the charging-discharging cycle of the battery with minimum overshoot and settling time. To verify the viability, the proposed system is first simulated in MATLAB and then verified at the OPAL-RT platform.

articleTitle: Power-Electronic-Controlled Electromagnetic Axial Bearings for High-Speed Electrical Machines: Status Review and Design Example
abstract: Contactless, electromagnetic bearings, controlled through power-electronic converters, are a good option for high-speed electrical machines. In addition to radial forces, the shaft of a machine also experiences axial forces due to reasons which are briefly indicated in this paper. This paper reviews the present status of power-electronic-controlled electromagnetic thrust (or axial) bearing (ETB) and reports a design example of the same. Being contactless, these bearings can operate at high speeds with a long life. Their lubrication-free operation makes them suitable for operation in vacuum, contamination-free or hazardous environments. This paper discusses the construction, operation, magnetic circuit analysis, and force-current characteristics of the ETB. Differential control of ETB is reviewed, including the overall control structure and dynamic models for position and current control. Electromagnetic design of an ETB to axially support a rotor of diameter 36 mm, delivering a maximum axial force of 1,600 N, is presented. The design steps include preliminary selection of major dimensions using design equations, followed by design iterations to achieve the specified performance. The final design is evaluated using 2-D and 3-D finite element analyses. Detailed modelling and controller design are reported for the ETB designed, whose performance is verified through simulations. Limitations of the present technologies and possible future research directions in various aspects of ETB are highlighted.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Approach to Assess Quantitative Resilience of Transmission Line During Cyclone
abstract: Power transmission system should be reliable and robust to meet the uninterrupted load demand. However, the performance of power system is affected when different system components are exposed to the extreme weather conditions. In this paper, quantitative assessment of component resilience is proposed by determining the transmission line failure under the natural disaster events like cyclone. Transmission line fragility curves are mapped with wind profile during cyclone to obtain the probability of failure of each transmission lines using Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) method. Available Transmission Capacity (ATC) and Load Not Served (LNS) are calculated to assess the resiliency of the standard IEEE 30 bus system. The results are promising to understand the impact of such events for assessment of infrastructural and operational resiliency studies during the planning stage.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Modulated Multilevel Converter at Variable Arm Inductance
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is an efficient converter due to its use in medium and high-power applications. In this manuscript, the output performance of modular multilevel converter is presented by varying the arm parameter (such as arm inductance and arm capacitance) as well as modulation index. This paper has also shown the comparative analysis of MMC by using different multicarrier modulation techniques at different modulation index. The total harmonic distortion (THD) analysis is shown here. It has been observed that the THD is improved by using phase shifted modulation technique as compared to phase disposition modulation technique. The phase shifted modulation approach is more efficient than other modulation techniques. The output performance of voltage and current analysis have been obtained.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Rank-Based Planning of the Distribution System with HOMER Integrated Weighted Sum Model
abstract: The integration of renewable energy into distribution systems has attracted global planners to deploy cost-efficient electric power distribution systems. This paper proposes novel distribution system planning with multi-criteria rank-based methodology. The planning incorporates cost, renewable energy contribution, and grid energy trading as a planning index. The system is first analyzed with HOMER to obtain the list of suitable combinations with the available resources and load demand. In the second step, the weighted sum model is applied to rearrange the obtained solution in a rank-wise manner. The proposed methodology provides the optimum configurations along with the global best solution with the rank-wise arrangement. The proposed method is applied with the meteorological data of Roorkee city to explore the efficient configuration suited for the distributed power system. The optimum configuration obtained is PV array with DG and a converter. Further, if WT is the choice of the planner, the size of PV array and DG can be reduced, and a 3-kW size of WT can be deployed. The proposed method efficiently explores the possible optimum solutions along with the global best solution with rank-wise arrangement for efficient and economical planning of the distribution systems.

articleTitle: Stochastic Eigen Analysis and Unified Control Mode for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Inverter Based Resources
abstract: A Grid-Forming Converter (GFMC) is a critical part for proper operation of an isolated microgrid (MG). Its aim is to generate voltage reference for rest of the inverter- based resources (IBRs) in the MG just like a traditional slack bus generator. To operate a GFMC in a d-q reference frame, single or dual loop proportional-integral (PI) controller is typically used. However, under system and grid parametric fluctuations, the above controller performs poorly. The voltage source converter (VSC) should operate for grid-tied (GT) as well as stand-alone (SA) mode to function as a grid following converter (GFLC) for power delivery to local loads where each mode has its own control loop. It should be seamless in providing an uninterruptible supply of power to the local load. Hence, for the addressable challenges, a non-linear model of both GFMC and GFLC that covers all system and grid parametric variables is devised along with stochastic eigen analysis. The suggested technique has an accurate model for the converter system which can cope with LC filter resonance and uncertainties more effectively where the need of any passive or active dampening methods is unessential. Simulations and tests were carried out to validate the suggested methodology. The simulation and experimental findings indicate that the suggested control strategy may be utilized to accomplish autonomous and smooth mode transitions even in the presence of norm-bound state uncertainty, as well as to offer resilience against grid impedance, system, and grid parameter fluctuations.

articleTitle: A PV-connected soft-switched synchronous Buck Converter for Electrical Vehicle
abstract: The paper presents a coupled inductor-based soft-switched DC-DC synchronous buck converter for electric vehicle applications. A coupled inductor is introduced to control the output voltage for broad load variations. The operation of two switches is carried out in a complementary manner. The short-circuiting problem during the outgoing and incoming switch at turn ON or turn OFF is rectified using a blanking circuit. This paper presents a complete design and analysis for a 300W soft switched synchronous buck converter, and the result obtained is verified with mathematical analysis and experimental results. The maximum efficiency obtained is 94.8%.

articleTitle: Investigation on Power System Stability with Integration of Renewable Resources
abstract: Penetration of high renewables impacts the steady state and dynamic operational behavior of a power network. The voltage profiling in a power system is depended on the reactive support provided by generating resources. The renewables generating resources has limited support for voltage control as compare to conventional power generating resources. The voltage stability is an inherent problem associated with high penetration of renewables in power systems. This article provides a steady state voltage stability analysis for an IEEE39 bus systems under high penetration of solar and wind power. Different operational scenarios with wind, solar and mix of both have been studied to investigate the voltage stability issues in this IEEE-39.The simulation work is performed in PSSE software using Newton-Raphson’s method to compute the power flow a for mix of generation from renewable resources. It is observed that the incremental percentage of electricity generated by renewable energy sources affects the voltage stability of the system and finally this may lead to voltage instability beyond a limited of renewables penetration.

articleTitle: Investigations on Sheath Voltage and Current During Short-Circuited Condition On a Cross-Bonded Cable
abstract: The Sheath is an eternal part of a cable, protects the insulation from moisture ingression, acts as an electrical shielding, and also a return path for load and fault current. Being grounded to at least any single point the cable sheath will always have either one of them or both types of phenomenon, the sheath voltage, and sheath current. To minimizes the losses in the sheath, the cable sheath was bonded in a cross-bonded formation., with the presence of a sheath voltage limiter (SVL). The SVL protects the cable sheath from transients and faults. In the lifespan of the cable, the most unavoidable event is the occurrence of faults. In the presence of a short-circuited fault at a particular phase, the sheath of the other phase may also get affected, causing deterioration in the condition of the cable. In this paper, a comparative study of sheath voltage and sheath current during a short-circuited fault at each phase was studied for both cases, in the presence and absence of SVL, the simulation study was carried out with circuit simulating software.

articleTitle: Battery Integrated MMC for Grid Connected Solar PV Application
abstract: Recently, a modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been employed to feed the power generated by renewable sources into the grid because of its inherent advantages like modularity, scalability, and high-power quality. Moreover, the infusion of energy storage elements, like batteries, into the MMC can provide a smoother and more reliable operation. A battery-integrated MMC-based solar PV inverter is introduced in this paper. The objective of the proposed topology is to offer an inbuilt energy storage system for MMC-based topology, especially when the MMC is employed to process the power generated by renewable sources. As renewable sources are stochastic, an inbuilt energy storage system can provide a smoother operation to any renewable energy-based power plant. Moreover, this architecture ensures the battery is an integral part of the system. This battery storage requires battery balancing that could be provided by active battery balancing through the MMC sorting algorithm. Further, the main DC bus of MMC is utilized as an evacuation port for solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays or any other renewable energy source.

articleTitle: Speed Sensorless Control of SynRL Motor for Electric Vehicle with Improved Third Order Generalized Integrator Flux Observer
abstract: The speed sensorless control of synchronous reluctance (SynRL) motor for electric vehicle with improved flux estimation based on third order generalised integrator flux observer(TOGIFO) is presented in this paper. Sensor reduction is crucial in electric vehicle (EV) drives based on synchronous reluctance (SynRL) motor in order to increase system dependability and robustness. Moreover, achieving seamless wide-range speed control without sensors is still difficult. When compared to the conventional stator flux linkage estimation method for accurate speed estimation, the sluggishness of the drive at low and high speeds of operation is mitigated by the improved speed and position estimation. A bi-directional DCDC Converter (B-DC) is used with the battery for improved performance of the system.The paper also discusses the improved battery performance for enhancing vehicle's range. The effectiveness of the presented system is verified through comprehensive MATLAB/Simulink validation.

Author Keywords: Third Order Generalized Integrator Flux Observer (TOGIFO)

articleTitle: Novel ECU Design Architecture using DSP and FPGA for Electric Vehicle
abstract: The foothold of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is increasing in the automobile industry and with it, the volume of Electric and Electronic devices has gradually increased. To control such equipment in an automotive Electrical Control Unit (ECU) is developed. The ECUs consist of Controllers, sensors, actuators, etc. A new firmware development control scheme using a Digital Signal processor (DSP) and Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) is proposed. Communication protocols such as Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) and Control Area Network (CAN) are used to communicate within the control board and the external world along with Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) for reliable communication. The new hardware design architecture and its obtained results are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Grid Interfaced Two Stage Solar System with Seamless Transition and Multifunctional Capability
abstract: This work presents an improved adaptive notch filter frequency locked loop (IANF-FLL) approach for solar photovoltaic (PV) system interfaced with three phase grid capable of working in both grid connected and islanding mode. The PV system produces active power and delivers to the loads coupled at PCC and excess power is delivered to the distribution grid. The voltage source converter executes various tasks such as mitigation of the harmonics, DC-AC conversion to supply the PV power to the AC load, generation of reference AC voltages during standalone mode of operation. Moreover, it is also capable to operate in the abnormal grid conditions such as DC offset and grid voltage distortion. Simulations are done on various dynamic conditions such as load unbalancing, grid voltages unbalance, PV insolation variation, standalone mode of operation and synchronization. The distortion levels of the grid currents achieved are well within the limits as recommended by the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: A Modified Zeta HPF AC-DC Converter with High Step- Down Gain using Switched Capacitor and Coupled Inductor Structures for LVEVs Charging Applications
abstract: A charger topology which is based on a modified zeta converter, for charging applications of low voltage electric vehicles (LVEVs) is demonstrated in this paper. As compared to the conventional Zeta converter with buck-boost gain, the topology presented in this paper uses a switched capacitor structure, that is able to give a wide voltage step-down gain in a single stage, between the AC input and low voltage battery packs. Moreover, the use of coupled inductor structure along with the design of inductor in discontinuous inductor current mode (DICM), further helps in reducing the size of magnetic components used in the circuit, thereby reducing the size of the charger as a whole. In addition, the DICM operation facilitates inherent power factor correction, and reduces the switching losses incurred in the conducting devices by incorporating soft switching. The converter presented in this work is able to give both good grid side performance, with unity power factor operation as well as low harmonic distortions in the input current, while maintaining a good charging profile at the battery end. Finally, the charger topology is simulated, through the proper design of its components; modes of operation and the performance of the charger along with its control circuitry is analyzed and verified. The results of the same are discussed in this work.

articleTitle: Improved LVRT Performance of Doubly-Fed Wind Generator System in Comparison with Neuro and Sliding Mode Control
abstract: The Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) in wind system is linked to the power-grid, which is vulnerable to significant grid failures. Because of the DFIG’s sensitivity to disturbances in the grid, designing of the controller is considered. In this article, the Feed-Forward Neuro-Second Order Sliding Mode (FFN-SOSM) controller and the Second Order Sliding Mode (SOSM) controller are compared for the Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) enhancement under voltage sag situation. Convergence in the sliding surface control is assisted by the use of higher-order switching functions in the FFN-SOSM. Importantly, controller benefits are such that reduction in chattering effect and minimized settling time for the system’s parameters as a result in the implementation of the FFN-SOSM method. With the assistance of MATLAB/SIMULINK, a comparison is made between the performances of the FFN-SOSM controller and those of SOSM controller, which is described in the existed research. The results of the simulation indicate that the "FFN-SOSM controller improved the LVRT capability of the DFIG-Wind Turbine (WT) system" when it is functioning under dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Seamless Control Approach Based on Modified Blake-Zisserman Function for Multiple DFIGs and SPV Arrays in a Grid-Interactive AC/DC Microgrid
abstract: Seamless control operation utilizing the generic modified Blake-Zisserman adaptive filter (GMBZ-AF) for a grid-interactive AC/DC microgrid is presented in this paper. The AC/DC microgrid structure comprises of multiple solar photovoltaic (SPV) arrays and multiple doubly-fed induction generators (DFIGs) for renewable power generation. The microgrid structure and its operational scheme are specifically designed to effortlessly enable further modular expansion with additional DFIGs and SPV arrays. Moreover, to enable a disruption-free power to the loads at various operation modes, and a seamless transfer among these modes, appropriate refinements are incorporated in the microgrid control strategy. These refinements, which are aided by the GMBZ-AF, are incorporated within the power converters' control strategies. Meanwhile, the primary operational objectives of the power converters remain unaffected. Verifications of the control strategy and the operational scheme with simulation analyses, are performed for a microgrid structure comprising three units each of DFIG and SPV array.

articleTitle: A Transformerless Power Conversion Unit for Grid Connected Solar PV System
abstract: For low voltage solar PV array, the conventional solar photovoltaic (PV) generation systems (GSs) employ low or high frequency transformers to match the voltage gain between AC mains and solar PV array. However, the utilization of transformers, causes significant increment in weight, size and losses in the system. Considering this, a transformerless solar PV power conversion unit (PCU), is presented in this work for residential roof-top applications. The presented PCU employs a two-stage power architecture with active bridge rectifier stage at front end and high gain DC-DC stage at back end. At back end, an extended gain boost (EGB) DC-DC converter is considered between low voltage solar PV array and high DC link voltage. The EGB DC-DC stage ensures desired voltage gain characteristics between solar PV array and inverters DC link, without the use of transformers. The voltage gain characteristic of presented EGB DC-DC converter is improved through switched capacitors to keep the overall weight of the PCU in check. Moreover, the input and output currents being continuous in nature, such feature is incorporated at the back-end stage of the presented PCU, to ensure effective maximum power point tracking at solar PV array, and reduced current ripples at DC link side. The low current ripples at DC link further reduce the size of DC link capacitor, and thus improve the reliability of overall system. Performance of presented transformerless solar PV PCU is analyzed through MATLAB Simulink modelling and relevant results are presented for performance justification.

Author Keywords: Extended Gain DC to DC Converters

articleTitle: Hierarchical Control of Stand Alone Microgrid for Peak and off-peak Hours Operation
abstract: Microgrid faces power quality issues like voltage and frequency unbalance due to its low inertia. The limited generation and heterogeneous load switching results in generation scarcity and hence affect the power quality. The intermittent availability of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) also hampers seamless power transfer. Thus, this paper presents a hierarchical control strategy where the primary control strategy maintains the voltage through a closed-loop inverter control technique and frequency through P-f droop mechanism. The secondary control implements a load management strategy to reduce peak demand and maintain frequency through Demand Side Management (DSM) by scheduling Thermostatic Control Loads (TCLs) and grid-tied electric vehicles. In recent scenarios, the usage of such loads is gaining ground hence scheduling results in balancing generation and demand. The voltage and frequency should be maintained adhere to IEEE 1547.1 by taking utmost priority to the customer’s comfort. The test system comprises of modified IEEE 13 bus system connected with PV, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), and Diesel Generator (DZ) for emergency purposes. The hierarchical control strategy is advantageous for peak and off-peak loading conditions with drastic load variation.

articleTitle: Impact of Cyber Attack on Control of Grid-Tied Power-Electronic Converter
abstract: Grid-tied voltage source converters (VSC) are the essential component in the integration of renewable energy sources (RES). As the RES are the need of present as well as the future generation, the role of VSC has become critical in the operation and control of modern and smart power grids. For the sake of reliability, as well as an economic point of view, these VSC require to work in coordination which necessitates communication link (which connects the sensors and controllers) to interconnect the VSC. However, with distributed control philosophy, control of VSC become vulnerable to cyber-attack, especially sensor attack. In this work, a few scenarios of cyber-attack on the control parameters of VSC and their impact on their performance are simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment and results are presented.

articleTitle: Multiple Feedforward with Feedback Based Control of Shunt Hybrid Active Filter for Fast Dynamic Performance
abstract: Dynamically varying industrial non-linear loads cause serious power quality problems that requires compensation strategies having fast dynamic response along with steady state performance as per standards. This study presents a novel approach to improve dynamical performance of shunt hybrid active power filter using multiple feedforward control at dominant harmonic frequencies coupled with feedback control. Multiple feedforward control involves introduction of active capacitance/inductance in series with passive LC filter at dominant harmonic frequencies. Dual compensation through parallel operation of feedforward and feedback control at dominant harmonic frequencies provides superior dynamic response compared to control strategies proposed in contemporary literature. The MATLAB Simulink<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> simulation shows the superior dynamic and steady state performance of the proposed technique which reduces the source current THD below 5% within 40 ms.

articleTitle: Deviation Settlement Mechanism for Improving Grid Frequency Regime in India
abstract: As invariably there would be some amount of deviation from the schedule, however small it may be, for a dynamic system like, power system, there is always a necessity to evolve Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) which is logically acceptable to the stakeholders. India being a developing country with resource crunches over the passage of time from hitherto isolated systems gradually developed state-grids, regional-grids, and then national-grid by 2013. During the journey with the availability of energy as well as power, excursion of frequency has narrowed down. Regulations too have allowed to achieve this. Over the years accordingly de facto DSM has undergone changes. Now with the present scenario and to progress further in this context in a simple, yet in an effective manner to be operative, a new mechanism has been illustrated based on primarily System Marginal Price (SMP), supplemented by a few feasible components. The latter include a few measurements in time slots of power, energy, frequency, etc. involving simple calculations.

articleTitle: Seamless Transitions of Variable-Speed Wind Generator in Standalone Microgrid
abstract: Control of a standalone microgrid during steady-state and transitions of constituent wind generator (WG) is presented. At PCC, a battery energy storage (BES) is connected via a bidirectional VSC, and a variable speed WG is connected directly. The PCC voltage and frequency are typically controlled by the VSC operating in grid-following (GF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) mode in presence of the WG and in grid-forming (GF) mode in absence of the WG. During every plug-in or plug-out operation of the WG, the operating mode of the VSC would switch aptly from one to another. A simple technique is presented in this paper, which allows to operate the VSC always in the GF mode, thus avoiding its mode switching. A pre-synchronizing loop handles the WG transitions. The principle of control scheme is presented and its efficacy is shown with help of simulation studies.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis between Perturb & Observe and Incremental Conductance techniques for MPPT in PV System
abstract: The paper offers a brief overview of the Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT and Incremental Conductance (INC) MPPT methods for maximizing the power output of a PV system connected to a rated resistive load. A PV panel can provide maximum power at a fixed operating point only, which is defined at a fixed voltage and current, called as maximum power point (MPP). So, a simulation is carried out to observe I- V & P-V characteristics of PV panel under varying irradiation and temperature conditions to test the genuineness of the MPPT techniques. Additionally, it compares these MPPT techniques based on control strategies, complexity, price, type of circuitry, number of control variables, and performance by utilizing data from simulations performed using the MATLAB Simulink R2022a software.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Digital Control Implementation of Unbalance Compensation in Three-phase Three-wire Stand-alone Inverters
abstract: This paper presents an FPGA-controlled three-phase inverter programmed for unbalance compensation in the output voltage of the three-phase inverter. The inverter output voltage becomes unbalanced because of the unbalanced load currents drawn by the unbalanced lads of the inverter. The unbalance compensation method mainly uses fundamental harmonic observers, which are designed to decompose a highly distorted voltage and current signal. These observers are embedded into the FPGA. FPGA is used along with other PWM-type controllers and input-output interfaces. The three-phase inverter fundamental output voltage is regulated by using a feedback control system, and a decoupled channel control mechanism has been employed to perform unbalance compensation. Two Cyclone FPGA chip implements the various signal processing steps in the closed loop inverter control methods.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking of Single-Phase Grid Connected PV based DC Microgrid System using Modified BBO Algorithm with PR Controller
abstract: The depletion of fossil fuels has made the world move toward distributed energy resources for power generation. Due to their simplicity of installation, photovoltaic (PV) systems are widely used for power generation. In order to serve the world of the ever-growing population with the increasing energy demand, it is important to extract the maximum power from PV solar systems to use them either in stand-alone or grid-connected mode. In the literature, various algorithms for the extraction of maximum power are explored. In this work, the Adaptive Quasi-Oppositional Differential Migrated Biogeography Based Optimization (AQDMBBO) algorithm is used for the novel application of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of a solar PV system, which is integrated with a single-phase grid. This algorithm exhibits simplified implementation with rapid convergence and maximum power extraction from solar panels. The efficacy of AQDMBBO is analysed by comparing its performance with the conventional BBO and Grey Wolf Optimization algorithms for MPPT of the given PV system. From the results, it is concluded that AQDMBBO exhibits higher accuracy, faster settling time and less duty variation for tracking the PV maximum power.

articleTitle: An Analysis of State of Art Maximum Power Point Tracking Techniques of the Solar Photovoltaic System Under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of state of art maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques applied to solar photovoltaic system (SPV) under partial shading conditions (PSC). This paper includes a description of partial shading problem, discussion on major challenges faced by SPV under PSC. This paper also presents the detailed classification of MPPT techniques along with their advantages and disadvantages under PSC at the conclusion section of the paper.

articleTitle: A Novel Resonant-Based Soft Switched Capacitor DC-DC Converter Topology for High Voltage and High Gain Application
abstract: Switched Capacitor Converters (SCC) are gaining popularity due to their advantages, such as high energy density, high efficiency, compactness, and minimal cost and their applicability under a broad range of applications. SCC’s are of two types-hard switched and soft switched. The hard switched converter possesses some severe drawbacks such as using high switching frequency and large value of capacitances to reduce current spikes during switching transients as there are no magnetic components associated with it. However, this adds to increased switching losses and considerably increases space consumption. Hence, a resonant-based soft switched converter is utilized which reduces the switching stresses by introducing Zero Current Switching (ZCS) operation into the converter. The switching frequency and overall capacitance size is also reduced. Several soft switched SCC are proposed in the literature, but they still have issues such as ZCS operation not applicable to all switching devices, usage of multiple inductances, device ratings not optimized for high voltage applications and so on. This paper proposes a novel resonant-based soft switched converter that utilises a single inductance on the input side to achieve ZCS operation of all the switching devices involved within the converter. The proposed converter also optimizes the ratings of the devices such that it can easily be used for high voltage and high gain applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Performance Investigation of a Solar PV Integrated DFIG System
abstract: The necessity of finding replacements for fossil fuels has become more widely recognized in response to increased energy demand. Therefore, experts are focusing on making renewable energy sources like solar and wind viable alternatives to long-term solutions for providing reliable and affordable electricity. This paper presents the framework for a hybrid system. The configuration comprises photovoltaic panels and a wind turbine that uses a direct current induction generator (DFIG) with controllers for the rotor side and grid side. The purpose of this paper is to conduct a performance analysis of a solar photovoltaic (PV) system that has been combined with a DFIG. A MATLAB/Simulink model of a 60 kW photovoltaic array and a 288 kVA DFIG system has been modeled to simulate and observe the system performance. The observation shows that the integration of a solar photovoltaic (SPV) system with a wind energy conversion system (WECS) based on a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) has the potential for demand-side power management. Finally, a real-time model is created using Opal RT to validate the hybrid system performance comparison under various operating conditions. Integration of PV systems with DFIG provides coordinated control, decreases operating costs, and boosts performance during the transfer of power flow.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control in Wind Penetrated Power System using a Novel IGWO based MPC Controller
abstract: This manuscript presents a novel methodology to solve the load frequency control (LFC) problem in the renewable energy-based power system network. Here, an Improved Grey Wolf Optimization tuned Model Predictive Controller has been proposed for the regulation of a 2-area thermal-thermal power system. The suitability of the proposed method has been verified after equating its transient response specifications with that of other existing approaches available in the literature concerning LFC problems. Further, the ARIMA modelling of practical wind speed data from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory has been considered using the Econometric Modeler tool on MATLAB. Subsequently, Monte Carlo simulations were employed to generate different stochastic scenarios of wind speed over the 24-hour range. And these scenarios were sampled and processed to generate the wind power which is plugged into area 1 of the LFC model. The resulting transient response suggests that the proposed controller keeps frequency oscillation within the safe range even in the presence of highly fluctuating wind speed.

articleTitle: An Analysis of State of Art Techniques for Solar PV Powered Water Pumping System
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of state of art techniques for solar PV powered water pumping systems (SPVP-WPS). The paper includes a detailed classification of SPVPWPS, discussion on important topologies of the SPVPWPS and discussion on major challenges faced by solar PV pumping systems. At the end of the paper, the simulated model of the standalone SPVPWPS using sensor-less BLDC motor drive without battery backup had been presented.

Author Keywords: Solar PV powered Water Pumping Systems (SPVPWPS)

articleTitle: Event Triggered Adaptive Primary Frequency Control Strategy for Low-Inertia Microgrids
abstract: This article proposes an event-triggered adaptive primary frequency control strategy for low-inertia microgrids with large penetration of renewable energy sources (RES). An adaptive control strategy strategy has been proposed which utilizes the event occurring information for providing fast frequency response (FFR) through operating point control of solar photovoltaic (PV) and/or power control through battery energy storage system (BESS) based voltage source converter (VSC). The control strategy utilizes the real-time information of solar PV power generation and event occurrence for providing FFR. Furthermore, a recovery control method is developed which can restore the power dispatch of solar PV based VSC and BESS based VSC to their initial operating state after providing FFR. The proposed control strategy has been evaluated on MATLAB/Simulink platform and performance of the proposed control strategy has been evaluated under different operating scenarios.

articleTitle: Analysis of Inter-area Oscillations-based Switching Attack in Large Power Systems
abstract: Inter-area oscillations-based switching attack is the new class of cyber-physical attack on power systems. In this type of attack, the adversary first obtains the inter-area mode details through a measurement-based approach. Then the adversary perturbs the load(s) at inter-area frequencies. In this work, inter-area-based switching attack characteristics and their effects on large power systems are analyzed. The Prony method is employed to estimate the inter-area oscillation mode frequencies and damping factor. Inter-area switching attacks are analyzed in the 4-machine 2-area, 10-machine 3-area and 16-machine 5-area power systems. It is observed that the system is driven to instability faster when switching attack is applied on the loads that are in the vicinity of the generators which are participating in the least-damped inter-area modes.

articleTitle: Impact of Plug-in Electric Vehicle and SVC in Congestion Management
abstract: With rapidly increasing sales of Plug-in Electric Vehicles, its penetration in a grid system is also increasing significantly. These Electrical Vehicles (EVs) not only act as loads to the grid, but can also be harnessed as integrated energy storage sources when working in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) mode to mitigate congestion. However, there have been limited studies on the comparison and impact of Plug-in Electrical Vehicles (PEVs) and Static VAR Compensator (SVC) in a grid system under congestion. This paper presents a systematic and comprehensive study of the impact of PEV and SVC and their performance comparison under congestion. The modeling of PEV in MATLAB/Simulink has been studied with respect to its mode of operation in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle mode (G2V). Different situations of congestion in lines and the impact of PEV and SVC on the system performance have been tested on the IEEE 5-bus system in MATLAB/Simulink. This will give a great insight to compare both the device’s performance under congestion conditions.

articleTitle: Economic Power Quality Enhancement for SEIG-Battery Hydro Standalone System Fed UAPF
abstract: The power quality (PQ) enhancement strategy is presented for a standalone system with battery supported and self-excited induction generator (SEIG) as source of supply. The main source of this standalone system is the power from the SEIG driven by the hydro turbine. However, when its operating at variable loads, as well as nonlinear loads, etc. the PQ issues are arise. So, the PQ indices are improved by integrating a universal active power filter (UAPF), which consists of two voltage source converters sharing common DC point. The voltage qualities are enhanced using the series active power filter (APF) of UAPF and maintains the harmonics free constant magnitude voltage across the load, regardless of any variation in generated voltage. Moreover, the power indices such as current harmonics, reactive power, power factor, etc. are improved by the shunt APF of the UAPF, simultaneously along with voltage quality enhancement. The distorted signals’ fundamental components are extracted using the adaptive generalized integrator (AGI) control algorithm, to estimate the reference signals and the switching pulses, to ensure the effective and efficient power quality improvement during various conditions. The IEEE standard 519 is being followed by the source currents and the load voltages.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Wind Energy Conversion Systems Based on PMSG for Maximum Power Extraction
abstract: This paper proposes a Permanent Magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) coupled wind energy conversion system (WECS). An exemplary illustration of a permanent magnet synchronous generator-fed with applied pitch angle control and gear drive control to acquire actual performances and compare the extracted power. The operation of WECS is a difficult task as its operation depends on many factor. One of the factor that affect the WECS system is availability of wind resources so overcome this problem and to make wind energy conversion systems more cost-effective, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) has been implemented to achieve maximum power. In this manuscript, the system has been implemented and a comparison has been done using Incremental Conductance (INC), Perturb & Observe (P&O), and Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA) MPPT techniques to improve system efficacy. System results have been simulated and validated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: P2P Transaction-Based Sharing Solution for Prosumers in Management of Cloud Energy Storage System
abstract: Self-generating consumers in the power system are known as Prosumers. Energy storage is the most necessary component of a self-generating future. Consumers have to use energy storage with renewable energy generation to take full advantage. With an increasing inclination towards renewable, not only the implementation of storage but also optimal and efficient use of storage is important. A solution to this idea is Cloud energy storage where users can rent capacity and use centralized storage virtually as if it was at their own premises. The management of the cloud energy storage systems (CESS) needs to be looked upon to optimally schedule the storage. P2P sharing has proved to be a better alternative in working with storage in the case of micro-grid/s. This explains main focus of this paper which is to develop an efficient capacity-sharing game-theory based algorithm. A case study of different models of CESS operation is considered. The comparison for consumers participating in different models of CESS operation and sharing of storage among the prosumers with solar generation is presented. Results prove the efficacy of the algorithm in terms of economic benefit to prosumers. The cost incurred in proposed mechanism is found to be reduced and depicted in tabular form with evident peak load reduction in the curves obtained.

articleTitle: An attempt to Design and Analysis of Multilevel Converter Topology for Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: Multi-level inverter system architecture and simulation has great potential to integrate and expand the solar photovoltaic system. The multi-stage inverter design is based on a number of topologies. The improved space vector pulse width modulation makes it possible both in qualitative and quantitative terms to improve systems efficiency and production. The device can be connected to the photovoltaic solar system. Generated DC power is link to the AC grid through the inverter and power transformers. Harmonic filters and massive, expensive, and lossy transformers are used in traditional inverters. Multi-level inverters with lower Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), inductor-free design and increased control range are a viable alternative to conventional inverters. They create a steps-like waveform that looks a lot like a sine wave. Smart grids can include a lot of distributed sources, and if those sources have low THD, filtering them at the common point of connection isn't as difficult. This paper proposes 19-level inverter with high boosting power and minimal THD. Phase Opposition Disposition Pulse Width Modulation (PODPWM) technique modulates the inverter switches for voltage balance and switching losses minimization. Simscape Power Systems' MATLAB Simulink toolkit used for simulation.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Speed Synchronization Techniques for Multi Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
abstract: In this paper, event-triggered control of various multi-motor synchronization techniques is proposed for efficient usage of network resources. The event-triggering strategy is employed on four motor synchronization techniques, viz., Master-reference control and Master-slave control. These synchronization techniques are developed for permanent magnet synchronous motor. The three-phase model of the motor is converted into two-phase model for simpler control. The PI-controllers are used to employ field-oriented speed control of the motor. Event-triggering condition is formulated, and the control law is implemented in an aperiodic manner, i.e., only when the event-triggering condition is reached. The proposed work shows that event-triggering strategy can be employed for multi-motor speed synchronization and the system stays stable. This leads to better utilization of communication, computational and energy resources. Lesser number of triggering pulses lead to efficient control. Also, a single event-triggering controller is sufficient for one motor synchronization technique.

articleTitle: Effect of Solar Radiation and Wind Flow on the IEC Based Thermal Modeling of Outdoor Power Transformers
abstract: The variation in daily environmental conditions have a notable effect on the thermal performance of the electrical machines, specially power transformers. The objective of this paper is to see the effect of solar radiation and wind flow external to the outdoor operating power transformers. The research work in this field involves the development of computational thermal models based on conventional International Electro-technical Commission (IEC) loading guide using appropriate software tools in order to determine the hot spot temperature. These thermal models are then modified by incorporating the effect of solar radiation and wind flow. The proposed method is validated using the operational data gathered from a 500MVA power transformer located at 400kV Grid Substation, Kankani, Jodhpur (Rajasthan, India). The comparative study between the conventional and modified thermal models helps in the reliable operation of power transformer and optimizes the use of forced cooling arrangements.

articleTitle: A Renewable Energy and Utility Grid Integrated MIMO Converter Interface for the Wireless Inductive Power Charging
abstract: In this paper, renewable energy and utility grid integrated Multi Input Multi Output (MIMO) converter interface is proposed for the Wireless Inductive Power Transfer (WIPT) charging of the Electric Vehicle (EV) energy storage systems. The proposed system uses front end converter to integrate the utility grid via DC-link. Later a buck-boost converter is employed to incorporate the DC-link of the utility grid and the Photovoltaic (PV) source. By operating the converter to achieve the maximum power from the PV source, the total DC-link output of the buck-boost the converter can be enhanced inherently and greater than individual sources. This is useful for achieving the increased power transfer of the WIPT system to charge the EV, since the two sources are connected in a cascade manner. Further, a boost converter employed to inject the wind source’s maximum power into the DC-link. The buck-boost converter’s total DC-link is connected to the WIPT system to transfer power using a high-frequency inverter on the primary system side and a rectifier on the secondary EV side. Another advantage of the proposed system is that it employs an easy control algorithm and does not necessitate any schemes to manage the power. Finally, the performance of the presented system is demonstrated using various simulations and hardware experimental results that are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modelling and Experimental Validation of a 6th order High Gain Z-source DCDC Converter using ARM based Microcontroller
abstract: This paper presents a z-source based high gain non-isolated DC-DC converter topology. The average space modelling is utilized to present the small-signal modelling and performance analysis of the proposed converter. Primarily, the state-space model is utilized to calculate the system matrices which will be further utilized to derive the transfer function. The gain parameters of the devised controller is estimated using the small-signal analysis. Moreover, both the steady-state and dynamic analysis of the proposed converter is also devised by using non-linear state-space model. The proposed converter topology is of sixth order because it is designed with the help of six energy storing elements. Finally, the proposed topology is modelled in MATLAB to test the performance and later it has been verified through laboratory scaled prototype. The closed loop performance of the developed converter is tested using ARM cortex based M-4 micro controller (STM32F407VGT6).

articleTitle: Generation Load Correlation in Power Grid Interconnected with RES
abstract: Integration of Distributed Energy Resources in conventional power grid have been a field of research and concern to enhance stability of the system. The work done is development of a Full-Scale "Comprehensive State-Space Model" for Micro-Grids consisting of Distributed Energy Resources (Inverter-based). All the sub-modules’ model is combined together to achieve a "Comprehensive State-Space Model" of complete Micro-Grid as a whole. The system parameters and "Operating-conditions" are given as an input, to obtain eigen values on "MATLAB Software". Eigen values concept of Control theory is utilized to perform the small signal stability analysis by the way of monitoring displacement in the trace of eigen values which basically is indicating damping of oscillatory-components in transient conditions. Sensitivity-analysis is carried out to arrive at conclusions of what all modifications are demanded in the design of controllers such that system stability can be improved.

articleTitle: Modulation of Self-Balancing Trinary Asymmetric Multilevel Converter For High Speed Drive
abstract: A three-phase cascaded H bridge multilevel inverter with a trinary ratio of asymmetry and 400Hz output frequency, for high-speed drives applications is presented in this paper. In the proposed work, DC buses of main bridges in all three phases are fed by DC sources and the rest of the bridges, i.e. auxiliary bridges are fed by capacitors. These capacitors are self-balanced and do not require any closed-loop control to balance their voltage. The paper explains the underlying concept of strategically using the available space vector redundancies to achieve natural convergence of capacitor voltages and presents the complete algorithm to include it in the modulation technique. Simulation of the proposed converter is carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK and results match well with the expectations.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Interior PMSM for Low Power EV Applications in Hilly Terrain
abstract: High power and high energy density is necessity of modern day electric vehicle (EV) system. Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (IPMSM) developed as a significant choice for EV applications due to its exceptional performance and compact size. A 4kW Electric vehicle drive system requires motor design to provide tractive effort for low power electric vehicle. In this paper 3-phase IPMSM is designed for hilly terrain using analytical method and proposed model is then validated with using Finite Element analysis using Ansys Maxwell 2D environment. The design process includes imperative assumptions and evaluates machine parameters. The design incorporates V-type magnet structure and NdFeB(N42) to utilized as rare earth material. The analysis results determine the effectiveness of anticipated machine design.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Solar PV Modules with Dust Accumulation for Indian Scenario
abstract: Solar energy has proven to be an assured front runner among renewable energy sources since it is clean, cost-effective and environment friendly. The output power and lifespan of a photovoltaic module are governed by a variety of factors such as incident solar radiation intensity, cell temperature, cloud and other shading effects, dust accumulation, weather conditions, geographical location, module orientation, etc. This work examines the impact of dust accumulation on the performance of the 5 kW photovoltaic system installed on the rooftop of the laboratory at Delhi Technological University. Performance analysis of the 5 kW photovoltaic system is carried out over 62 days such that the panels were left naturally uncleaned for the first 31 days and then cleaned on a regular basis for the following 31 days. Performance parameters such as performance ratio, capacity factor, system energy yield and reference energy yield are derived. The performance analysis results of the practical 5 kW system were later compared with the PVsyst software results.

articleTitle: Multimode Control of a Grid Interactive Microgrid With Parallel Inverters Interfacing Independent PV Arrays
abstract: This paper presents a microgrid with two parallel inverters linking independent photovoltaic arrays (PVAs) to the grid, with boost converters being the intermediate stage facilitating peak power withdrawal. Under the normal scenario of healthy distribution network, both the voltage source converters (VSCs) of the microgrid stay linked with the grid, and deliver a predefined power, regardless of the prevalent generation levels and load demands. This control over the exchanged power is made possible by the use of a battery energy storage (BES). In case an anomaly is found with the grid voltages, the microgrid is delinked from the utility network, and the main VSC switches to a grid forming operation, whereas the slave VSC operation is unperturbed. The BES stabilizes the standalone operation by acting as a source or sink, as per requirements. The main VSC also establishes transient free reconnection at grid revival. The microgrid control is resilient against non-ideal grid voltages, and also prevents the local nonlinear loads from deteriorating the grid power quality.

articleTitle: Circuit Averaging Approach for Impedance Modeling of Source and Load Converter with Bidirectional Converter
abstract: This paper presents a circuit averaging approach to model the ac small-signal impedances of the dc/dc converter system used for integrating source, load, and battery. These impedances are further used for the stability analysis using Middlebrook’s criterion. The impedance transfer functions for closed loops are obtained under both the charging and discharging scenario of the battery. The simulated impedance frequency responses are given to verify the mathematical model.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation on Two Wing Ring Type Armature with Inductive Type Electromagnetic Launching System
abstract: Electromagnetic launching is one of the intriguing features studied by numerous research institutions worldwide. Electromagnetic launching is only possible when flux lines flow through the moving object. The moving flux lines flow creates magnetic interference with the control components inside it. This is the major drawback of electromagnetic launching technology. To overcome this drawback, a different combinations of armature shape and electromagnetic principles are needed. This paper concentrates the use of electromagnetic induction principle for propelling the object. A Two-wing Ring type Armature is designed, which can accommodate any type of material inside the ring. The magnetic field is induced on to the wings of the armature. This helps is reducing the amount of magnetic interference into the material which needs a propulsion. This paper presents a ring-type armature feasible for EM launching. This phenomenon has shown positive results in reducing the electromagnetic interference on the sensitive electronics components of the projectile. The Armature 3D model has been developed in ANSYS 2021 Electronics Workbench. This paper helps in understanding various magnetic characteristics of the two wing ring-type armature.

articleTitle: Modified Boost Converter for High Power Applications
abstract: Lithium-ion battery is one of the competent sources for electric vehicle. In this work, the lithium-ion battery is integrated with Multiphase Boost Converter and is compared with conventional boost converter. The proposed method is tested on software and hardware platforms in order to test its efficacy. The comparison is done on the basis of maximum duty ratio, size of inductor and source ripple current. The results show that the size of inductor get reduced to half to that of conventional boost converter. The proposed system will reduce the ripple current coming to the source and increase the power transfer from the source to the load.

articleTitle: Parallel Converter Fed High-Performance PMSM Drive with Reduced Circulating Current Meant for High-Speed Applications
abstract: High-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives are preferred for high-speed electric vehicle applications due to high power density and efficiency. Standard PMSM drive (SPD) consists of a voltage source inverter (VSI) feeding PMSM in vector control mode. Such motor drives operate at a fundamental frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>) more than 750 Hz and power levels ranging up to a few tens of kW (≥ 50 kW). In order to restrict switching energy losses, switching frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf>) is restricted below 10 kHz. Thus, pulse number (P) (i.e., ratio of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sw</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>) drops below 15 over moderate and high f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>. Consequently, drive performance deteriorates significantly in terms of total harmonic distortion in line current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THD</inf>) and peak-peak torque ripple $(\tilde {\tau} )$. An optimized interleaving angle is identified to confine high frequency circulating current (i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cir</inf>) within ratings of power converter while maintaining nearly minimum I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THD</inf> and $\tilde {\tau}$. To achieve a reduction in i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cir</inf> without compromising on I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THD</inf> and $\tilde {\tau}$, this paper further proposes coupled inductors based PMSM drive-II. Performance of proposed PMSM drives I and II are compared with the SPD in terms of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">THD</inf> and $\tilde {\tau}$. Simulation results pertaining to three-phase, 50 kW, and 916 Hz PMSM drive are presented in the paper to validate the propositions.

articleTitle: Design of Discrete IMC Controller for Mitigation of Cyber-Attacks
abstract: This paper proposes the Internal model control(IMC) design technique to mitigate cyber-attacks such as gain attacks, deception attacks, or man-in-middle (MITM) attacks. The plant will be volatile when the gain attack is introduced in the forward path of the communication channel. We replace the existing PI controller with the proposed IMC design-based controller to mitigate the after-effects of cyber-attacks. Further, it is also observed that the stationary error introduced by the deception attack was removed entirely. The tracking of reference input is achieved with this proposed IMC-based compensator. The validation of the proposed approach is carried out on the servo system and simulated in a MATLAB-SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Improved Binary Bat Algorithm for Optimally Placing Multiple DGs in RDN
abstract: Identification of optimal location for placing distributed generators for the mitigated power losses and upgraded voltage profile in radial distribution network is presented in this article. Load flow solution is obtained using Backward-Forward Sweep method. Improved Binary Bat algorithm, as optimization technique, is used to evaluate the possible best location and magnitude of dispersed generators. Analysis is done by simulating over IEEE-33 and IEEE-69 bus system. Results signifies the loss reduction with voltage profile improvement.

articleTitle: Real Time Adjustment to Mitigate the SPV Forecasting Errors with BESS and EV - An Utility Case Study
abstract: Adherence to schedules prepared by operators has become more challenging with an increase in the penetration level of non-dispatchable resources at different scales. The inherent variability and uncertainty associated with such resources including Solar Photo-Voltaic (SPV) based generation poses real-time scheduling challenges. Irrespective of the forecasting technique adopted, errors will always persist. Hence, the power flow must be optimized in real-time. The capability of dispatchable resources including Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) and Electric Vehicles (EVs) can be leveraged to absorb the forecast errors in real-time so that the schedules pre-specified by operators can be effectively followed. A problem formulated as an Optimal Power Flow (OPF) is presented in this paper to mitigate SPV forecasting errors for the Snohomish County Public Utility District (SnoPUD)’s Arlington Microgrid in the USA. Real world datasets have been used for testing and validation of the developed approach for the Arlington Microgrid with two test cases 1) grid connected mode and 2) islanded mode of operation. Detailed results are also presented in the article, taking two different seasonal (Spring and Summer) variations into account.

articleTitle: Active Charge Equalization of an ‘m×n’ Battery Stack in Electric Vehicles during Charging, Discharging, or Isolated Condition
abstract: In this paper, an active battery charge equalization technique for Electric Vehicles using an ‘m×n’ battery stack is proposed and analyzed. The proposed configuration allows to achieve voltage and current balance of all the batteries in the battery stack during charging, discharging, or idle situations. A fourth-order battery integrated dc-dc bi-directional converter with a battery stack is operated to implement charging, discharging, and isolated conditions for the battery stack. The whole equalization process as well as an analysis of the effect of duty ratios on equalization time and equalization current of the battery stack is explained. The obtained results were found to be consistent with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Charge Equalization Techniques used for Battery Management System of Residential DC Nano-Grids: A Brief Review
abstract: The increased popularity of Renewable Energy Sources and Electric Vehicles, the demand of battery systems has been increasing exponentially. Due to these various shortcomings of installing battery stack to the systems are being more and more reported. The biggest shortcoming of using batteries is the problem of the mismatch of the State-of-Charge of the batteries, which can lead to reduced power transfer capacity of the batteries, reduced efficiency, more losses, reduced life spans, and even potential fire hazards. This paper presents a comprehensive study and comparison of the numerous charge equalization techniques present in the literature with the aim to aid the study and further exploration of the shortcoming presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Frequency Control in Power Systems via Reduced Order Model Based GADRC Approach with Communication Time Delay
abstract: A higher-order power system is prone to deviate from the quality performance due to the frequent load fluctuations, parametric uncertainties in the existing system, variations in the model structure, etc. Because of this, the frequency stability in such power system becomes a prime factor of concern, and an appropriate control strategy must be employed to accomplish the load frequency control (LFC). Since the full order controllers encounter significant computational and structural setbacks, lower order controllers are utilized to investigate the performance of such high-order power systems. In the present study, the reduced order generalized active disturbance rejection control (RDGADRC) approach incorporating the model order reduction technique has been developed and employed for the single area power system. The presented technique inherits the advantages of two well-established GADRC and model order reduction techniques. The efficacy of the proposed technique is authenticated based on the communication delay handling capacity, robustness against parametric variations, and disturbance rejection capability.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch Using Honey Badger algorithm (HBA)
abstract: For the stability, dependability, and security of the power system, reactive power must be adequately monitored and managed. Reactive power dispatch is a difficult mixed integer and nonlinear problem that is essential for maintaining safe voltage levels and increasing system efficiency. To lower transmission line losses and load bus voltage variations, reactive power dispatch controls the positions of transformers load tap changers, capacitors reactive power injection, and the voltages of slack buses and PV buses. The Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch (ORPD) problem has been solved in this paper using a novel meta-heuristic approach known as the Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA). Utilizing the IEEE 30-bus system, the applied single-objective deterministic ORPD approach is evaluated and contrasted with previously published research articles for the reduction of voltage deviation and power loss.

articleTitle: Optimal Procurement of Energy using Combined GA-OPF Technique in Deregulated Power Sector
abstract: This paper suggests a combined Genetic Algorithm (GA)-Optimal Power Flow (OPF) method that may be used to procure the energy. This paper suggests a market-based mechanism for Renewable Producers (RP) to clear energy in a deregulated environment. For energy procurement and/or cost minimization, the sequential cleaning technique has been considered. The proposed mixed GA-OPF technique for obtaining the required service has been investigated utilizing a modified IEEE-30 bus test equipment. The Optimal Power Flow (OPF) technique, which takes into account all transmission restrictions and power flow limits, is used to define and solve this optimization problem. When compared to Conventional Power Producers (CPPs), it is evident that the proposed approach using RPs offers lower procurement costs.

Author Keywords: Optimal Power Flow and Renewable Power Producers

articleTitle: Three Phase High-Resolution Multilevel Converter for STATCOM Application
abstract: Quaternary ratio based Multilevel Inverter (MLI) for the application of reactive power compensation is explored in this paper. The asymmetrical MLI topology comprises of three H- bridges per phase and maintained 16:4:1 ratio of asymmetry. Three voltage sources of high voltage bridge are replaced by floating capacitors. In presented converter, one floating capacitor and twelve switches are used per phase. The capacitor’s voltages are balanced using a close- loop scheme by taking the power from grid. The reactive power injection from leading to lagging is verified by a step change in the reactive current reference in the control scheme. The simulation is performed in MATLAB/Simulink for verification of the application.

articleTitle: Operation of Solar PV Grid Integrated Dual VSC-BES with Multimode Seamless Transition Capability
abstract: This paper presents a solar photovoltaic array (SPVA)- battery energy storage (BES) based three-phase microgrid (MG), which performs in two modes, i.e., grid interactive mode (GIM) and standalone mode (SAM). In GIM, an adaptive-based block-sparse least mean square (BS-LMS) algorithm is utilized for generating the triggering pulses to the voltage source converter1 (VSC1) and eradicating the harmonics in grid currents. Under the grid fault condition, the MG shifts towards the SAM. Here, two parallel connected VSCs are utilized for power quality enhancement and power flow management. Moreover, the primary VSC1 connects the SPVA to the common coupling point (CCP) and the secondary VSC2 connects the battery at the CCP. The maximum power extraction (MPE) is achieved by controlling the DC-DC boost converter (BC) by using the maximum power point tracking (MPPT)-based perturb & observed (P&O) algorithm. The MG control strategy is verified through simulated results.

articleTitle: An Energy Management Algorithm for Parallel Hybrid Energy Storage Based Isolated and Grid Connected System
abstract: The inclusion of supercapacitor with battery not just improves the system performance but also enhances the reliability and life cycle of the system. A parallel connection of supercapacitor and battery based Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) reduces one DC/DC bi-directional converter and control circuitry associated with it. However, a proper scheme to utilize this parallel HESS in an AC/DC microgrid is not present in the literature. This article presents an energy management algorithm for a parallel connected battery supercapacitor based HESS for residential smart building application. The article also presents the design of HESS for a smooth transition of battery current. The proposed energy management algorithm consider multiple modes of operation depending on grid peak pricing, state-of-charge of battery, grid connectivity, MPP mode of PV, and load shedding of non-critical load in deficit power mode. The reference current for all the available sources are generated using the proposed algorithm and the control is designed to operate the system uninterruptedly in all the modes of operation. Further, the dynamic and steady state performance of the proposed control strategy has been verified through theoretical analysis and digital simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A study on future decarbonization pathways using various PV technologies with dual-axis tracking
abstract: The performance of three distinct PV technologies, i.e., rystalline Silicon (c-Si), Cadmium Telluride (CdTe) and Copper Indium Selenium (CIS) technology, enabled with a dual-axis tracking system, has been compared and analyzed for the six different climate zones of India. The analysis was conducted using photovoltaic geographical information software (PVGIS).
